text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Opposition parties called for a nation-wide strike on Saturday to protest against the imposition of new taxes.
- The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry rejected the new economic measures announced by the government on Tuesday.
- The Sindh provincial government raised power tariffs 1.7 percent for all consumers.
- Pakistan is likely to reduce wheat imports to 1.8 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July-June) from 2.3 million tonnes last year, said the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
- Local gold prices shot up roughly 300 rupees per 10 grams after the depreciation of the rupee on Tuesday.
- A Pakistan-Canadian joint venture for local production of canola edible oil will be established in Pakistan.

- A two-member team from the U.S.-based credit rating agency Moody's Investors Services Inc left Pakistan after two days of talks with officials of the Ministry of Finance, the State (central) Bank of Pakistan and senior executives of private financial firms.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif said imposing taxes without consent of the National Assembly (lower house) was in clear violation of the constitution.

- The budget deficit will remain at 4.6 percent of gross domestic product despite the recent economic package and the government will have to use privatisation proceeds of 14 billion rupees to reduce it to four percent of GDP, sources said.
- The review mission of the International Monetary Fund will arrive in Pakistan on October 26, sources said.
FINANCIAL POST
- The government will approach friendly Arab states to arrange a $682 million loan required for debt repayments.
THE FRONTIER POST
- North West Frontier Province Chief Minister Aftab Sherpao said local bodies elections would be held in December.
THE NEWS
- Investment Minister Asif Ali Zardari returned to Pakistan and said he was not scared of facing an accountability process.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
